newsitem.title: USA: Chinese officials seek U.S. investment.
newsitem.headline: Chinese officials seek U.S. investment.

text.p: Chinese officials were looking for U.S. investment in 177 projects, ranging from building highways to computer manufacturing, at a meeting with American business executives here on Wednesday.

An 82-member Chinese delegation traveled to San Francisco for the one-day symposium on investment opportunities in central and western China, described by organizers as one of the largest events in U.S.-China economic exchange history.
Similar meetings were due to be held in New York and Atlanta later this month.

Delegation leader Xie Shusheng said China's central and western areas had made great progress in recent years but lagged behind fast-growing coastal areas because they were "in a relatively weak position in terms of transportation and telecommunications."
However, the central and western regions had a very large industrial base, abundant natural resources and a large supply of labor, he told a news conference.
"The Chinese government stands ready to support investment in this area," said Xie, president of the China Association of Enterprises with Foreign Investment.
The aim of the meeting was to explain investment policies in central and western China and to bring together U.S. investors and projects from those regions, organizers said.
The Chinese delegation was offering Americans the chance to invest in 177 projects, valued at hundreds of millions of dollars, in nine provinces. Investment is usually on a joint venture basis.

The projects include highway, railway and harbor construction; oil, gas and metal mining; power plants; amusement parks and tourism; textile manufacturing; car and car parts manufacturing; computer hardware and software manufacturing; real estate development and food processing.

Michael Bianco, president of the U.S.-China Finance and Investment Council, a grouping of U.S. and Chinese financial institutions which was one of the sponsors of the meeting, said he was happy to see dialogue continuing between the United States and China.

"It's meetings like this we must have in greater number. More importantly, we need to follow up on these meetings and the relationships that are developed through these kinds of conferences," he told the news conference.
The Chinese delegation included policy makers from the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, senior officials from provincial trade and investment bodies and business leaders.
